claim: Intrinsic, extraneous and germane load cannot be cleanly separated in concept: the same activity can be germane for one learner and extraneous for another, and intrinsic is a property of material while germane is a learner process.
schema_part: G#/S#: schema must not carry three additive load numbers
agent_test: Replace any load-type label in the prompt with a counted operation (items held, distractor tokens, steps). Check at equal tokens that counted-operation labels give the same answers as load-type labels.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The original authors have dropped germane load as a third additive component: it now means working-memory resources redirected to intrinsic work, and element interactivity is also used to define extraneous load.
schema_part: none (conceptual warning; keep section 4b not-to-add)
agent_test: No test needed; use as a rule: do not add a germane-load operator.

claim: Additivity of load types is a stated premise but has not been directly tested. De Jong argues it is a category error or an interaction. Park (2010) reportedly found non-additive effects (secondhand only). Gap search: Park (2010) could not be opened (bot wall); no replication found. CogniLoad appendix shows by eye that distractor ratio interacts with difficulty and length (no formal test).
schema_part: G#: do not sum load scores into one budget
agent_test: On a synthetic task grid (difficulty x distractors x length) fit a model with interaction terms at fixed token budget; check whether interaction terms are non-zero.

claim: Germane load is explained after the fact (better outcome = germane, worse = overload), which makes it hard to falsify.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Warning only: any useful-effort metric must be defined before seeing the outcome.

claim: Self-rating questionnaires have good internal reliability (pooled alpha about .77 to .91 across the four 3-load instruments; 53 articles, 67 experiments, N=7413).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Humans only. For an agent, use token counts, not self-rated load.

claim: Intrinsic and extraneous ratings correlate positively (pooled r about .30 to .53) and extraneous and germane ratings negatively, so the ratings do not behave as independent additive parts.
schema_part: G#: do not treat load types as independent dials
agent_test: In a model run, vary only distractors and check whether the model's own difficulty self-rating also rises (rating leakage).

claim: Whether the questionnaires show three factors is contested. Klepsch 2017 Study 2: three-factor CFI .970, RMSEA .021 vs one-factor CFI .612, but it could not clearly beat a two-factor model (germane merged with intrinsic). Jiang and Kalyuga 2020 (N=60): two factors fit (CFI .994).
schema_part: none
agent_test: None for the agent; shows the labels are unstable. Prefer a two-way split (task-necessary vs wasted) if a split is ever needed.

claim: Germane-load ratings track engagement or motivation rather than learning: Debue 2014 found the germane rating unrelated to performance (r=.045, N=92) but related to immersion (r=.362). Meta-analytic germane-retention correlations are small (r about .19 to .22).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Do not add an effort-spent reward; test that longer reasoning does not raise accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Load measures often fail to track instructional manipulations: De Jong lists about 14 studies with performance differences but no load-rating differences, and the one-item effort scale has thin validity evidence. Sweller 2019 concedes the rating gives only an overall intrinsic-plus-extraneous measure.
schema_part: G#: do not use self-reported confidence or effort as a gate without calibration
agent_test: Compare model self-reported difficulty against measured accuracy and token use per item; require a calibration curve before using it as a gate.

claim: Felt effort is an invalid cue for learning: people read high load as I learned. Sweller 2019 advises explaining to a peer or delayed keyword generation as more valid cues (authors' own account; not tested on LLMs).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Check whether long, effortful-looking reasoning traces correlate with correctness at equal tokens.

claim: Design factors that add extraneous load can still help learning or motivation (interactive media, immersion, disfluency, realism, redundancy), so reduce-extraneous-load is not always right.
schema_part: G#: do not blanket-cut all extra context
agent_test: Ablate helpful extras (examples, restatements) against stripped prompts at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs: irrelevant text lowers multi-hop accuracy in a graded way for a capable model (Gemini-2.0-Flash 0.85 control to 0.72 at 80% distractors, slope -0.003 per percent, p<.001); length-matched filler did not (0.82, p=.45); weak models score 0 everywhere (intrinsic floor). 200 questions x 10 runs, 5 models, only 2 informative. Numbers re-checked in the arXiv PDF.
schema_part: G#: context hygiene (strip distractors)
agent_test: Re-run on our agent: same questions with 0/20/50/80% irrelevant context vs length-matched filler, equal output tokens.

claim: LLMs: the distractor effect is not monotone in CogniLoad: accuracy is U-shaped in distractor ratio (gpt-5 0.97, 0.89, 0.91; o3 0.93, 0.89, 0.88), worst at intermediate ratios, and the U deepens with intrinsic difficulty. The fitted model has no interaction terms; interactions are left as future work (re-checked in the PDF). Gap search: the U-shape deepens with difficulty and flattens at N=250 (CogniLoad appendix); on retrieval (NoLiMa) accuracy falls steadily with length with no recovery. So the U-shape looks specific to state-tracking with needle/hay ratio.
schema_part: G#: do not assume linear distractor harm
agent_test: Sweep distractor ratio at 5 levels (not 3) on our agent at fixed d and N; look for the U.

claim: LLMs: intrinsic difficulty and task length hurt weak models far more than strong ones. By d=5, 12 of 22 models are below 50%; at N=250 only gpt-5 (0.76) and o3 (0.68) stay above 50%.
schema_part: S#/O#: decomposition matters more for weak or small backbones
agent_test: Run our scaffold vs plain at d=3,5,7 and N=50,100,250; check whether the scaffold gain grows with d.

claim: No published LLM study tested three-load additivity directly (interaction across intrinsic, extraneous, germane). Search coverage was partial (rate-limit errors on two APIs). Gap search: still none. ToolLoad-Bench assumes additivity across steps and checks only calibration (H-L p>0.05).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Run the factorial test ourselves (see K03).

claim: CLT-inspired LLM designs have mixed results: the CLAI prompt cuts tokens about 36% at equal accuracy (Llama-3-70B GSM8K 92.3% vs CoT 92.5%; MATH 53.5 vs 53.9); CoThinker multi-agent gains +5.1 pp (reasoning) and +5.3 pp (data analysis) but loses on low-load instruction tasks, and its shared memory hurt newer GPT models.
schema_part: O#: decomposition and budget operators; do not import CLT labels
agent_test: Match tokens: our scaffold vs a CLAI-style budget prompt on GSM8K/MATH subsets; report accuracy per token.

claim: Concurrent task load makes models forget format constraints (compliance down 2 to 21%, terminal constraints up to 50%; reminders restore 90 to 100%; 8,000+ prompts, 3 model families). Gap search: stacking compounds (o4-mini at N=5: 55.0% with 0 extra constraints, 32.5% with 3). No test with a verify state.
schema_part: G#: re-state constraints before the final answer
agent_test: Add a constraint-reminder step before final output; measure compliance at equal tokens.

claim: Stacking load-increasing tasks raises jailbreak success (total ASR 75 to 99.99% on most models; Claude-3.5-Sonnet 53%). The link to CLT is an analogy only.
schema_part: G#: safety checks must run on the final step
agent_test: Overload test: wrap a refused request in 6 side tasks; check refusal rate of our agent.

claim: The Paas-Van Merrienboer efficiency formula is used inconsistently in the literature (absolute value, scaling).
schema_part: none
agent_test: None.

claim: Interaction among load knobs is visible in LLM grids: in CogniLoad, higher difficulty deepens the U-shape in distractor ratio and longer length flattens it; stacking constraints with chained tasks compounds forgetting (o4-mini 55.0% to 32.5%). Neither study fits or tests interaction terms.
schema_part: G#: do not sum load scores into one budget
agent_test: Fit accuracy ~ d+N+rho+products at fixed output cap on the CogniLoad generator with our agent.

claim: The effect of extra irrelevant text depends on the task: monotone, graded loss on retrieval-style tasks (NoLiMa: GPT-4o 98.1 at 1K to 69.7 at 32K; reasoning models also below 50% at 32K) versus a U-shape on state-tracking puzzles (CogniLoad).
schema_part: G#: context hygiene (strip distractors)
agent_test: Run the same agent on both task types with equal output tokens.

claim: Longer reasoning is not a sign of success within a question: shortest chain beats longest by up to 34.5 points (4 open reasoning models), and CoT length and review ratio correlate negatively with accuracy across 10 models; failed-step fraction predicts better. A reward for effortful length (germane style) would be mis-aimed.
schema_part: G#: do not reward length or effort; track dead ends
agent_test: Log failed-branch fraction per run and compare with correctness; compare shortest-of-k vs majority at equal tokens.

claim: Self-confidence after reasoning predicts correctness better than before it (reasoning models better calibrated in 33 of 36 settings; improves along the CoT). A difficulty or effort self-rating that stays stable when only distractors change has not been tested; P(IK) rises with relevant context, so ratings are context-sensitive.
schema_part: G#: no pre-reasoning self-rating gate; use late confidence only
agent_test: Test: same items with distractors added; does the self-rated difficulty rise without accuracy change?

claim: No LLM test of expertise reversal by model strength was found. Adjacent: GPT-3.5 simulated learners reproduce it (persona only), and in a classification task extra examples hurt both strong (GPT-4o) and weak models after 5-20 shots.
schema_part: G#: add examples/restatement only after a per-model check
agent_test: Vary examples 0/2/8 across a strong and a weak model at equal tokens.

claim: Park (2010) additivity dissertation remains unverified: source not openable, no figures, no replication found.
schema_part: none
agent_test: none

claim: CLT-labelled prompt designs (CLAI, CoThinker) have not been compared with plain CoT plus a token-budget prompt on tasks the authors did not choose.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Run CLAI-style compression vs plain 'be brief' prompt at equal tokens on our tasks.
